title: Exceptional points and cusp singularities in relativistic stellar oscillations with causal bulk relaxation
abstract: Causal relativistic hydrodynamics introduces relaxation degrees of freedom that elevate a quadratic oscillation problem to a cubic non-Hermitian spectral pencil. We study its exceptional-point (EP2) curves and an $A_3$ cusp, and construct an exactly solvable radiating wave--relaxation problem with a P\"oschl--Teller potential and an Israel--Stewart channel. Using hyperboloidal coordinates, outgoing Siegert conditions become endpoint conditions. For the aligned transport profile and away from discrete resonant couplings, we prove that the complete quasinormal point spectrum decomposes into a tower of sector cubics, with radiative damping rates determined by the boundary-value problem. The resulting EP2 and cusp geometry is therefore realized by genuine quasinormal eigenvalues. Multiprecision bordered-Newton calculations certify the degeneracies and their square-root and cubic-root splitting laws. Under a controlled parity-preserving deformation of the viscosity profile, the fundamental EP2 survives over a finite parameter window before annihilating with a partner and moving into complexified parameters; the cusp also persists. For dense matter, we derive a criterion independent of the relaxation time: $(v_{\rm FR}/v_\beta)^2 \ge 1+\Theta(\gamma)$, where $\Theta(\gamma)$ is the minimum coupling ratio along the EP2 locus. For weakly radiating compressive modes, $\Theta\simeq 8$, requiring $v_{\rm FR}\gtrsim 3v_\beta$. Internally consistent nucleonic Urca matter misses this threshold by more than two orders of magnitude. Exotic-matter comparisons are indicative benchmarks rather than same-equation-of-state exclusions. The radiating model is not a relativistic TOV-star perturbation; establishing the mechanism in a realistic star remains open.

title: $\Lambda$-Gravity from Entropy
abstract: The Gravity from Entropy (GfE) theory treats the metric of spacetime as quantum operators and proposes the GfE action for gravity. The GfE Lagrangian is given by the Geometric Quantum Relative Entropy (GQRE) between the true metric and the metric induced by the matter fields and curvature. The theory leads to modified gravity equations and predicts the emergence of a dynamical cosmological constant $\Lambda_{\mathcal{G}}$. In the low energy, small curvature limit the GfE gravity equations reduce to Einstein equations with vanishing cosmological constant, i.e. in the weak field linear approximation $\Lambda_{\mathcal{G}}$ vanishes. In this work, we propose a generalisation of the GfE theory, called $\Lambda$-Gravity from Entropy ($\Lambda$GfE). Following a thermodynamic approach, we introduce a Lagrange multiplier $\Lambda$ to define the local volume of the theory. By enforcing local Weyl stationarity of the $\Lambda$GfE action modulo the volume constraint of the theory, we derive the equation for $\Lambda$. The $\Lambda$GfE equations of motion include two dark energy contributions: the emergent and dynamical contribution given by $\Lambda_{\mathcal{G}}$ plus a constant contribution given by $\Lambda$ where $\Lambda$ can be identified with the cosmological constant in the low energy small curvature limit. While this theory cannot predict the exact value of $\Lambda$, here it is shown that the vacuum contributions to the dressed stress-energy tensor cancel from the trace-free equations of motion of the $\Lambda$GfE theory. Within the GfE framework, the $\Lambda$GfE also offers a novel interpretation of the dark energy terms, with potentially testable consequences for cosmological observations.
